title: Finite tame pro-etale sheaves have finite root-level etale models
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic a positive prime $p$, let $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be regular Noetherian and separated of finite type over $k$, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ be equations of the labelled branches of a reduced strict normal crossings boundary, with $r\geq0$ [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Put $f=\prod_i t_i$ (empty product $1$) and $V^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]$. Let $F_0$ be a sheaf of sets on $V^\circ_{\mathrm{proet}}$ that becomes constant with finite, possibly empty, values on a pro-etale covering [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Assume that at every geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, its pullback to the punctured full prime-to-$p$ parameter-root tower of $\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is finite constant: here only the parameters vanishing at $\bar v$ are rooted, transitions for $m\mid n$ send the $m$th root to the $n/m$th power of the $n$th root, and puncturing inverts their product [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], [def-sfb-strict-local-kummer-tame-module].

Then $F_0$ is the pro-etale sheaf represented by a finite etale $P\to V^\circ$; this representation identifies sheaf maps and geometric fibres with the corresponding maps and fibres of finite etale covers [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], [def-weil-geometric-point]. At every $v\in V$, the vanishing $t_i$ extend to a regular system of parameters in $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. There are $n>0$ prime to $p$ and a finite etale $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}B_n$, where $B_n=B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_i$, whose restriction after inverting $f$ is identified with the pullback of $P$. For every $B$-algebra $H$, putting $H_n=H\otimes_B B_n$, the scheme $E_n=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B_n}\operatorname{Spec}H_n$ is finite etale over $\operatorname{Spec}H_n$, and its restriction $E_n\times_{\operatorname{Spec}H_n}\operatorname{Spec}H_n[1/f]$ represents the pullback of $F_0$ to $\operatorname{Spec}H_n[1/f]$. These assertions include $r=0$ and the empty sheaf, with no condition on the degree of $P$. Pullbacks use [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image].

proof.text:
Write $X=V^\circ$. For $d\geq0$ let $T_d=\operatorname{Isom}(\underline{\{1,\ldots,d\}},F_0)$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$; isomorphisms glue uniquely, so $T_d$ is a sheaf. On a trivializing member $U$ with model a finite set $S$, a map $\underline{\{1,\ldots,d\}}	o F_0$ is $d$ sections, since a finite constant sheaf is the coproduct of $d$ copies of the final sheaf; after a common covering refinement these sections and the inverse images are constant, and the inverse equations are exactly those of a bijection. Thus $T_d|_U$ is the constant sheaf of the finite set of bijections $\{1,\ldots,d\}	o S$, empty unless $d=|S|$ and a singleton for $d=|S|=0$. So each $T_d$ is locally constant, hence $T_d\simeq
u_X^*H_d$ for an etale set sheaf $H_d$ by local classicality. Let $T=\coprod_dT_d$ (sheaf coproduct). As $
u_X^*$ is a left adjoint, $T\simeq
u_X^*H$ with $H=\coprod_dH_d$, compatibly with the summand inclusions. $T$ restricts on $U$ to the constant sheaf of the nonempty set of orderings of $S$, so $T$ is locally classical with sections on a pro-etale covering, and the sections clause gives an etale covering $\{Y_i	o X\}$ with $T(Y_i)
eq\varnothing$. For etale $Y$, $
u_{X,*}$ is evaluation at $Y$, so the comparison unit gives $H(Y)\simeq T(Y)$ and $H_d(Y)\simeq T_d(Y)$, naturally in $Y$ and compatibly with the inclusions $H_d	o H$. A section of the etale sheaf coproduct $H$ over $Y_i$ lies, on an etale covering $\{Y'	o Y_i\}$, in single summands $H_d(Y')$: sheafification is locally surjective, because the subsheaf of locally-presheaf sections receives the presheaf map, and the universal property makes it everything. Hence $T_d(Y')
eq\varnothing$, i.e. $F_0|_{Y'}\simeq\underline{\{1,\ldots,d\}}$ on these etale members $Y'$. So $F_0$ has finite constant models on an etale covering of $X$.

source.place: Lemmas 5.1.2 and 5.1.4, printed p.34; explicit finite-frame argument analogous to Corollary 5.1.5

proof.text: Apply local classicality also to $F_0$ itself, obtaining $F_0\simeq\nu_X^*G$ for an etale set sheaf $G$. On each etale trivializing member $U$ of step 1, comparison and restriction commute: both right adjoints evaluate a sheaf at the same etale $U$-scheme, hence their left adjoints agree. Constants are inverse images from sets and are preserved by these left adjoints. Full faithfulness of $\nu_U^*$ therefore identifies $G|_U$ with the finite constant model of $F_0|_U$. Apply finite-locally-constant sets descent to $G$: it supplies a finite etale $P\to X$ and $G\simeq h_P$.

The inclusion of the etale site in the pro-etale site preserves finite limits and coverings. Both sites are subcanonical. Apply representable inverse image to this inclusion: $\nu_X^*h_P\simeq h_P$ on the pro-etale site, so step 2 represents $F_0$ there. Yoneda identifies all maps between these represented sheaves with $X$-morphisms between their finite etale schemes. At a geometric point, the comparison-stalk isomorphism reduces the fibre assertion to $G$. On the etale splitting cover of step 1 both the stalk of $G$ and the geometric fibre of $P$ are the same finite set of labels; evaluation of a section at the point is this identification. These local identifications agree on overlaps because evaluation commutes with restriction, giving the asserted natural fibre identification.

proof.text: Fix $v\in V$. The SNC parameter criterion gives parameters $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ in $A=\mathcal O_{V,v}$ with boundary ideal $(u_1\cdots u_s)$. The regular-local factorization lemma says that these $u_j$ are distinct prime elements. Since the $t_i$ are equations of the labelled reduced branches, the principal ideals $(t_i)$ for the vanishing labels are precisely the distinct minimal primes $(u_j)$ of this product ideal: in a domain a prime containing a product contains a factor. Equality of nonzero principal ideals in a domain gives $t_i=a_i u_{\sigma(i)}$ for units $a_i$. Replacing the corresponding parameters by these unit multiples preserves generation of the maximal ideal and its number of generators. It follows from the definition of a regular system of parameters that the vanishing $t_i$ extend to one. Off the boundary the list is empty.

source.place: Tags 0BI9 and 0BIA, definition-strict-normal-crossings and lemma-strict-normal-crossings, local branch equations

proof.text: For any scheme map $a:T\to X$ and finite etale $Q\to X$, the pro-etale inverse image of $h_Q$ is $h_{Q\times_XT}$: apply the representable inverse-image theorem to the base-change functor defining $a^{-1}$. Its finite-limit and covering conditions are precisely those recorded in the inverse-image definition, and subcanonicality holds for both pro-etale sites. In particular apply this to each punctured strict-local full parameter-root tower. The hypothesis says that the resulting represented sheaf is finite constant. A finite constant sheaf is a finite coproduct of final sheaves; the finite-coproduct comparison identifies it with the sheaf represented by the corresponding finite disjoint union of the tower. Yoneda turns this isomorphism into a scheme isomorphism. Consequently the pullback of $P$ to every one of the towers in the root-extension lemma is a finite disjoint union of copies of that tower.

source.place: Tag 04D3; proetale.tex Tag 09A5 and finite coproduct comparison for disjoint open-and-closed summands

proof.text: Apply the SNC tame root-extension lemma to $V$, the given labelled equations, and $P$. The regularity, Noetherianity, separated finite type over $k$, and positive characteristic hypotheses are those of the item. Step 4 verifies its parameter hypothesis, and step 5 verifies its exact tower-splitting hypothesis, with the same active labels and power transition maps. It gives $n>0$ prime to $p$ and finite etale $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}B_n$, together with $Z[1/f]\simeq P\times_X\operatorname{Spec}B_n[1/f]$. No degree condition is used by that lemma.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i)-(iii), printed pp.133-134; finite-root consequence supplied by the cited node

proof.text: For an arbitrary $B$-algebra $H$, base change of $Z$ is finite by finite-morphism permanence and etale by etale base change. Therefore $E_n\to\operatorname{Spec}H_n$ is finite etale. Pull the isomorphism of step 6 back to $\operatorname{Spec}H_n[1/f]$. Associativity of fibre products, or its two projection equations, identifies its right side with $P\times_X\operatorname{Spec}H_n[1/f]$. The representable inverse-image comparison identifies the sheaf of this last scheme with the pullback of $F_0$. Thus it is the restriction $E_n[1/f]$ that represents this sheaf. Nothing here requires $H$ to be Noetherian or flat.

If $r=0$, then $f=1$, $B_n=B$, and $n=1$, $Z=P$ work. If $F_0$ is empty, use $P=\varnothing$, $n=1$, $Z=\varnothing$; the frame of its empty fibre remains the unique empty ordering, so the descent argument includes it. If $V$ is empty all constructions are the unique empty covers. Arbitrary finite fibre cardinalities and disconnected schemes were allowed throughout, and no step requires the degree of $P$ to be prime to $p$.
